course: Linear algebra, one idea a morning

sources.lay: David C. Lay, Linear Algebra and Its Applications, 5th ed.
sources.bronson: Bronson & Costa, Linear Algebra: An Introduction
sources.syllabus: Stanford OHS UM51A course schedule, lessons 10-38

days.title: Vectors
days.big_idea: A vector is an arrow from the origin and a list of numbers at the same time; adding and scaling mean the same thing in both pictures.
must_cover: vector as arrow and as column
scalar multiplication stretches, shrinks and flips
days.centerpiece: Two sliders for a and b sweep a·v + b·w and its tip paints the whole plane.

days.title: Linear combinations and span
days.big_idea: The span of some vectors is every place you can reach by scaling and adding them.
must_cover: two non-parallel vectors in R^2 span the plane
parallel vectors only span a line
span of two vectors in R^3 is a plane through the origin
is b in Span{v1, v2}? as a question about solving an equation
days.centerpiece: A 3D camera orbits while two vectors sweep out a plane, then a third vector either pokes off it or lies flat in it.

days.title: Systems of equations and row reduction
days.big_idea: Row operations change the equations without changing the solution set, so we simplify until the answer is readable.
must_cover: a linear system and its augmented matrix
row echelon and reduced row echelon form
no solution / one solution / infinitely many, shown as intersecting lines
days.centerpiece: Each row operation happens in the matrix while two lines on the plane pivot but keep crossing at the same point.

days.title: Matrix times vector
days.big_idea: Ax is a linear combination of the columns of A, using the entries of x as the weights.
must_cover: Ax = b is the same question as 'is b in the span of the columns'
vector equation, matrix equation and augmented matrix are one problem
days.centerpiece: The columns of A fly out as arrows, get scaled by x1 and x2, and snap tip-to-tail into Ax.

days.title: Matrices are transformations
days.big_idea: A matrix moves every point of the plane, and its columns record where the two basis arrows land.
must_cover: linear transformation: grid lines stay straight, parallel and evenly spaced, origin fixed
columns = images of e1 and e2
days.centerpiece: The whole grid morphs under a shear, then a rotation, with i-hat and j-hat highlighted and their landing spots written into the matrix.

days.title: Matrix multiplication is composition
days.big_idea: AB means do B first, then A; the product's columns are A applied to B's columns.
must_cover: AB as composition read right to left
AB ≠ BA shown with a rotation and a shear
days.centerpiece: Shear-then-rotate and rotate-then-shear play side by side and end in different places.

days.title: The inverse of a matrix
days.big_idea: A⁻¹ is the transformation that undoes A, and it exists exactly when A doesn't squash space flat.
must_cover: definition A A⁻¹ = A⁻¹ A = I
solving Ax = b as x = A⁻¹b
singular matrix collapses the plane to a line
days.centerpiece: The grid transforms under A, then plays the transformation backwards under A⁻¹; a singular matrix flattens it and there is no way back.

days.title: Elementary matrices and computing inverses
days.big_idea: Every row operation is multiplication by an elementary matrix, so row-reducing A to I builds A⁻¹ along the way.
must_cover: E is I with one row operation applied
A is invertible iff it is a product of elementary matrices
days.centerpiece: [A | I] row-reduces step by step; each step is also shown as a small grid move, and the right half fills in to become A⁻¹.

days.title: LU decomposition
days.big_idea: A = LU records elimination once, so solving Ax = b for many right-hand sides becomes two quick triangular solves.
must_cover: L stores the multipliers used in elimination
solve Ly = b then Ux = y
days.centerpiece: Elimination multipliers drop out of A one by one and land in the lower triangle of L while U forms above.

days.title: What is a vector space?
days.big_idea: Anything you can add and scale by the usual rules is a vector space, including polynomials, functions and matrices.
must_cover: the axioms as closure + ordinary algebra rules
examples: R^n, polynomials P_n, 2x2 matrices, functions
a non-example that breaks an axiom
days.centerpiece: Polynomial curves add and scale on a graph exactly the way arrows do, shown side by side.

days.title: Subspaces
days.big_idea: A subspace is a flat piece through the origin that you can never leave by adding or scaling.
must_cover: three-part subspace test: contains 0, closed under +, closed under scaling
lines and planes through the origin
span of anything is a subspace
days.centerpiece: Vectors on a line through the origin add and scale and stay on it; on a shifted line, their sum jumps off.

days.title: Span as the smallest subspace
days.big_idea: Span{v1,…,vp} is the smallest subspace containing those vectors, and a spanning set is a recipe for the whole space.
must_cover: checking whether a set spans R^n with row reduction (pivot in every row)
adding redundant vectors doesn't grow the span
days.centerpiece: Adding a third vector to a plane in R^3: if it's in the plane nothing grows; if not, the span inflates to all of space.

days.title: Linear independence
days.big_idea: Vectors are independent when none of them is redundant, meaning the only way to combine them to 0 is with all weights 0.
must_cover: dependent means one vector is a combination of the others
more vectors than dimensions forces dependence
days.centerpiece: Three arrows in R^3; when one drops into the plane of the other two, the parallelepiped they span flattens.

days.title: Basis
days.big_idea: A basis spans the space with no redundancy, so every vector has exactly one address in it.
must_cover: spanning set theorem: trim a spanning set down to a basis
days.centerpiece: The same point gets its coordinates read off two different skewed grids.

days.title: Coordinates and dimension
days.big_idea: Every basis of a space has the same size, and that number is the dimension.
must_cover: coordinate mapping is an isomorphism to R^n
all bases have the same number of vectors
days.centerpiece: A polynomial turns into a column of coefficients and back, showing P_2 behaves exactly like R^3.

days.title: Column space and row space
days.big_idea: The column space is everything A can output; its pivot columns form a basis.
must_cover: Col A = span of columns = range of x ↦ Ax
basis for Col A: pivot columns of the original A
row space and why row ops preserve it
basis for Row A: nonzero rows of echelon form
days.centerpiece: A 3x2 matrix sends the whole plane into R^3, and the image is a tilted plane: the column space.

days.title: Null space
days.big_idea: The null space is every input that A crushes to zero, and it is always a subspace.
must_cover: finding a basis from free variables in parametric form
solutions to Ax = b are a shifted copy of Nul A
days.centerpiece: A projection squashes the plane onto a line; a whole line of vectors collapses onto the origin and glows.

days.title: Rank and nullity
days.big_idea: Every input dimension either survives into the output or gets crushed: rank + nullity = number of columns.
must_cover: rank = dim Col A = number of pivots
nullity = dim Nul A = number of free variables
dim Row A = dim Col A
days.centerpiece: Column-by-column tally: each column lights up as pivot or free, and two bars fill to the total n.

days.title: The invertible matrix theorem
days.big_idea: For a square matrix, a dozen different-sounding conditions are all the same fact: A doesn't squash any direction.
must_cover: equivalent statements: invertible, n pivots, Nul A = {0}, columns independent, columns span R^n, rank n, x ↦ Ax one-to-one and onto, det ≠ 0 (preview)
how each links to the next
using it to decide invertibility fast
days.centerpiece: A web of equivalent statements lights up all at once when a matrix is invertible and goes dark together when it is singular.

days.title: Linear transformations between vector spaces
days.big_idea: A linear transformation is any map that respects adding and scaling, and that includes differentiation.
must_cover: examples: matrix maps, differentiation on P_n, transpose
days.centerpiece: The derivative acts on a family of polynomials and visibly respects adding and scaling them.

days.title: The matrix of a linear transformation
days.big_idea: Pick a basis for each side and any linear map becomes a matrix; column j is where basis vector j lands, in coordinates.
must_cover: the matrix of d/dx on P_2
days.centerpiece: Each basis polynomial goes through d/dx, gets converted to coordinates, and drops into its column of the matrix.

days.title: Change of basis
days.big_idea: A change-of-basis matrix translates coordinates from one grid's language to another's without moving the vector.
must_cover: computing it by row reducing [c1 c2 | b1 b2]
days.centerpiece: One fixed arrow with two overlaid grids; its coordinates in each grid count up simultaneously.

days.title: Kernel
days.big_idea: The kernel is everything T sends to zero, and T is one-to-one exactly when the kernel is only zero.
must_cover: kernel of d/dx on P_n is the constants
days.centerpiece: Two different inputs land on the same output, and their difference is shown to live in the kernel.

days.title: Image (range)
days.big_idea: The image is every output T can make; the rank-nullity theorem splits the input dimension between kernel and image.
must_cover: dim ker T + dim range T = dim V
days.centerpiece: Input space splits into a kernel direction that collapses and a complementary direction that maps onto the image.

days.title: The determinant measures area
days.big_idea: det A is the factor by which A scales areas (volumes in 3D), with a sign that says whether orientation flips.
must_cover: unit square maps to parallelogram of area |det A|
2x2 formula ad − bc derived from the picture
days.centerpiece: The unit square stretches into a parallelogram while a live counter tracks its area, passing through zero as it flips.

days.title: Computing determinants
days.big_idea: Cofactor expansion computes any determinant, and row operations change it in three predictable ways.
must_cover: expansion along any row or column
triangular matrix: product of the diagonal
effect of each row operation on det
det(AB) = det A det B, det Aᵀ = det A
days.centerpiece: A 3x3 expands along a row with the checkerboard of signs, and each 2x2 minor highlights as it's computed.

days.title: Determinant properties and Cramer's rule
days.big_idea: Because det is linear in each row and flips sign on swaps, it follows the rules that make det(AB) = det(A)det(B) and Cramer's rule work.
must_cover: proof sketch of det(AB) = det A det B via area scaling
days.centerpiece: Applying B then A multiplies the area twice, drawn as two successive scalings of the same square.

days.title: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues
days.big_idea: An eigenvector is a direction A only stretches, never turns: Av = λv.
must_cover: eigenvalue λ as the stretch factor
days.centerpiece: The grid transforms and most arrows knock off their lines, but the eigenvectors stay on their spans and glow.

days.title: Finding eigenvalues
days.big_idea: λ is an eigenvalue exactly when A − λI squashes space, so we solve det(A − λI) = 0.
days.centerpiece: Slide λ along a number line; the transformed grid of A − λI collapses flat exactly at the eigenvalues while a plot of det(A − λI) crosses zero.

days.title: Properties of eigenvalues
days.big_idea: Eigenvalues tell you trace, determinant and what powers of A do.
must_cover: trace = sum of eigenvalues, det = product
eigenvalues of A^k, A⁻¹, A + cI
eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are independent
days.centerpiece: Repeatedly applying A to a vector; it swings toward the dominant eigenvector's line.

days.title: Generalized eigenvectors
days.big_idea: When there aren't enough eigenvectors, a chain of generalized eigenvectors fills the gap: (A − λI) pushes each one down the chain.
days.centerpiece: A shear has only one eigen-direction; a second vector gets pushed by (A − λI) onto that line, then to zero.

days.title: Diagonalization
days.big_idea: If you have enough eigenvectors to make a basis, A = PDP⁻¹, and in that basis A just scales each axis.
days.centerpiece: P⁻¹ rotates the eigen-grid onto the axes, D stretches along them, P rotates back, which reproduces A.

days.title: Diagonalizing a linear transformation
days.big_idea: Choosing an eigenvector basis makes the matrix of a linear transformation diagonal.
must_cover: [T]_B for eigenvector basis B is diagonal
similarity as the same map in different coordinates
days.centerpiece: The same transformation is shown in the standard grid (messy) and the eigen-grid (pure stretching).

days.title: Symmetric matrices and the spectral theorem
days.big_idea: Symmetric matrices always have real eigenvalues and perpendicular eigenvectors, so they are rotations of pure stretches.
must_cover: eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal
spectral decomposition as a sum of projections
days.centerpiece: A unit circle becomes an ellipse whose axes are exactly the perpendicular eigenvectors.

days.title: Dot products and orthogonality
days.big_idea: The dot product measures how much two vectors point the same way; zero means perpendicular.
days.centerpiece: As one vector rotates, the shadow it casts on the other grows, shrinks, hits zero at 90 degrees and goes negative.

days.title: Orthogonal projection
days.big_idea: Projecting onto a subspace finds its closest point, and the leftover piece is perpendicular to the subspace.
must_cover: projection onto a subspace with an orthogonal basis
days.centerpiece: A vector drops a perpendicular onto a plane in 3D; the error vector glows at a right angle.

days.title: Gram–Schmidt
days.big_idea: Gram–Schmidt straightens any basis into a perpendicular one by subtracting off shadows one vector at a time.
days.centerpiece: Each new vector loses its projection onto the previous ones and swings to perpendicular.

days.title: Least squares
days.big_idea: When Ax = b has no solution, project b onto Col A and solve that instead: AᵀAx = Aᵀb.
must_cover: geometric meaning: projection onto column space
days.centerpiece: Data points with a fitted line; residual segments shrink as the line springs into its best position, and a side view shows b projecting onto Col A.

days.title: Quadratic forms
days.big_idea: xᵀAx describes bowls, saddles and ridges, and the eigenvalues of A tell you which one you have.
must_cover: quadratic form from a symmetric matrix
constrained max/min on the unit circle
days.centerpiece: A 3D surface morphs from bowl to saddle as one eigenvalue changes sign.

days.title: The singular value decomposition
days.big_idea: Every matrix is a rotation, then a stretch along the axes, then another rotation: A = UΣVᵀ.
days.centerpiece: The unit circle rotates, stretches into an ellipse and rotates again, followed by an image rebuilt from more and more singular values.
